title: Silver and gold have I none (Acts 3)
word: Silver and gold have I none
hookLine: the lame man walks and leaps into the temple
tomorrow: two fishermen face the council. why can't they stop talking?

lines: A CUP AT A RED LIGHT.
cards: At a red light, someone holds out a cup, and your hand goes to the cup holder for coins, or it doesn't. Peter and John are walking up to the temple at the hour of prayer.
At "the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful" sits a man who has never walked, carried there day after day to ask for alms. He asks them. Peter has no money.
So he gives something else, and it starts with his eyes.

teach.b: Peter stops, and he looks. "And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us." The man looks up, "expecting to receive something of them."

teach.h: SUCH AS I HAVE GIVE I THEE.
teach.b: Then the line: "Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk." Such as I have. Peter can't give what he doesn't have, and he doesn't pretend to.

teach.h: A HAND, AND ANKLES THAT HOLD.
teach.b: Then a hand: "he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength." And the man doesn't stroll in politely.

"He leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God." One to tell a friend tonight: the man who sat outside the gate every day is now inside it, and loud.
A crowd runs together, staring, and Peter turns the stare away from himself: "why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?"
He points them to Jesus' name instead. The gift was never Peter's to show off; it was his to hand on. And it began with the cheapest thing anyone has to give: a long, straight look.

how: Some Christians quote Peter's 'such as I have give I thee' when giving time or skill rather than money, and Acts 3 is read in some churches in the Easter season.

o: no money, but I give what I do have

games.q: a neighbor's car won't start, and he asks to borrow money for a tow. you're broke this month, but you know a bit about engines. what fits Acts 3?
o: say you can't lend money, then offer to look at the engine.
apologize that you're broke and wish him luck.
promise money next week so he isn't let down.
games.why: Peter didn't pretend to have silver. he said so plainly, then gave what he had: a look, a hand, and the name he trusted.

practice: Count on your fingers five things you have that cost nothing to give: a minute, a skill, a name you remember, a ride, a laugh. Pause on each one as you breathe.
Let the last finger rest on the one you could hand to someone this week.

wordCard.voice: Silver and gold have I none. Peter's words at the gate: no money, but what he did have, he gave.

orig.note: Greek: silver and gold. Acts 3:6, the first words of Peter's answer at the gate.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: walking and leaping, through the gate he used to sit outside. Day six of Acts.
